traitor.title: Traitor's Tome
traitor.text:
### Setup
- Your explorer stays in the game but has turned traitor.
- You are possessed by the greedy spirit of your Aunt Edwina and are obsessed with your Bequests.
- Your Bequests are the item cards and omen cards you hold that can be traded or stolen. A card counts if it can be either traded or stolen, even if not both (for example, the Armor and Blood Dagger count, but the Bite doesn't). Count them to get your Bequest total; it changes as you gain and lose cards.
- When the heroes are ready to continue: if your Bequest total isn't higher than the highest Bequest total of any single hero, draw item cards until it is.
- If any of your traits are below their starting values, raise them to their starting values. Then increase one of your traits by 1.

### Rules
#### Every turn as the traitor
- If you both begin and end your turn as the traitor, you may increase one of your traits by 1.

#### After every explorer's turn
- If your Bequest total is equal to or less than any other explorer's total, every explorer rolls dice equal to their own current Bequest total (maximum 8, minimum 1).
- Each explorer in a room with an item symbol adds 1 to their result.
- The explorer with the highest result becomes the traitor. On a tie, the tied explorer closest to your left becomes the traitor.
- When you stop being the traitor, you must give one of your Bequests, chosen at random, to the new traitor, together with the Traitor's Tome. You become a hero and may read the Secrets of Survival text. You may not reveal any details of the Traitor's Tome to the other heroes.
- If you die while you are the traitor, the heroes roll as described above to determine who is possessed by Aunt Edwina next.

> Note: the printed heading, "You must do this on every turn", leaves open whether the roll for the next traitor happens after every explorer's turn or only after the traitor's. The heading above carries the official correction.
> Resolution (official): errata. The check happens at the end of every explorer's turn; the FAQ changes the heading to "You must do this on every explorer's turn". Source: https://www.dropbox.com/s/3y34f1s2tn6o4mx/Widow%27s%20Walk%20FAQ%20KB%2012.6.161.pdf?dl=0

#### Special attack
- Once on your turn, you may try to take back Bequests stolen by the "thieving little mice" by making an attack using any trait.
- If you defeat the other explorer, roll on the Bequest Disposition table. If you don't defeat them, the attack has no effect.

#### Bequest Disposition
Roll 1 die.

| Roll | Result |
|---|---|
| 0 | The attacked explorer discards a random Bequest. |
| 1 | Steal a random Bequest from the attacked explorer. |
| 2 | Steal a Bequest of your choice from the attacked explorer. |

#### Items and omens
- You may not willingly trade or drop item cards or omen cards.
- If you are ever in a room with any dropped item cards or omen cards, you must pick up all of them.
- When you die, drop all your Bequests in an item pile. For each Bequest dropped for any reason, roll 1 die; on a blank, that Bequest is discarded.

### Traitor wins when
- You end your turn holding all the Bequest cards, or
- all other explorers are dead.

### What you know about the heroes
- The heroes take your (most recent) body's death as license to rummage through your house and wreck your collection. You'll need to retake what's yours, and maybe find a better body to inhabit along the way.

heroes.title: Secrets of Survival
heroes.text:
### Setup
- Set aside the Item Pile tokens.
- If the house has fewer rooms with an item symbol [horned skull symbol] than there are explorers, draw room tiles and put the ones with item symbols into play until there are as many item rooms as explorers.
- Each hero draws an item card. Then each hero counts their total number of item cards and omen cards that can be traded or stolen. (A card that can be traded but not stolen, or stolen but not traded, counts. For example, the Armor and Blood Dagger count, but the Bite doesn't.) These cards are your Bequests; your Bequests change as you gain and lose cards.
### Rules
#### How to capture Edwina's spirit
- If the traitor ever has no Bequests, Edwina's spirit starts searching for a suitable Bequest. While that is the case, any hero in a room with an omen symbol [raven symbol] may say "You are free" and drop a Bequest to draw out Edwina's spirit. Her spirit is pulled into that heirloom, and the heroes win.
#### Special attack rules
- As usual, the traitor is the only explorer you may attack and steal from normally.
- However, instead of your normal attack, once during your turn you may try to steal a Bequest from another explorer in your room, either by persuading them it isn't worth dying over (a Sanity attack) or by telling an old story about Aunt Edwina that proves the Bequest means more to you than to them (a Knowledge attack).
- If you make this attack while in a room with an item symbol, add 1 die to your attack.
- This attack deals no damage. If you defeat the other explorer, roll on the Bequest Disposition table. If you don't defeat them, the attack has no effect.

> Note: the printed rules leave open whether a hero can still steal from the traitor by dealing 2 or more damage in a normal attack, and whether the Bequest attack is in addition to a normal attack. The first two bullets above carry the official correction.
> Resolution (official): errata. You may attack the traitor and steal from them normally, and the Bequest attack replaces your normal attack for the turn. The FAQ rewrites Special Attack Rules this way; it labels the change as Traitor's Tome text, but the rewritten section is the heroes' one. Source: https://www.dropbox.com/s/3y34f1s2tn6o4mx/Widow%27s%20Walk%20FAQ%20KB%2012.6.161.pdf?dl=0
#### Bequest Disposition
- Roll 1 die.

| Roll | Result |
|---|---|
| 0 | The attacked explorer discards a random Bequest. |
| 1 | Steal a random Bequest from the attacked explorer. |
| 2 | Steal a Bequest of your choice from the attacked explorer. |

#### Special item and omen rules
- You are overcome with greed: you may not willingly trade or drop item cards or omen cards, except as described in How to Capture Edwina's Spirit.
- Whenever you are in a room containing any dropped item cards or omen cards, you must pick up all of them.
- If you die, drop all your Bequests in an item pile.
- For each Bequest you drop for any reason, roll 1 die; on a blank, that Bequest is discarded.
> Note: Read literally, "for any reason" would include the Bequest dropped in How to Capture Edwina's Spirit (which ends the game at once), so the roll matters only for other drops such as dying.
### Heroes win when
- You trap Aunt Edwina's spirit inside an heirloom in her collection (see How to capture Edwina's spirit), freeing yourselves and the house from her influence.
### What they know about the other side
- The traitor is possessed by Aunt Edwina's greedy spirit, which seems set on repossessing the most interesting pieces of her macabre collection — at least the pieces the heroes hold.
